$comment: Systems that are not types, stats or creatures. Mirrors SPEC.md sections 4.2 (crit), 9 (move delivery) and 12 (energy, affection). Anything marked status 'unspecified' has a shape but no numbers yet, deliberately -- see OPEN_QUESTIONS.md.

crit.$comment: Crit chance rises with level and then stops. Moves and abilities modify chance and damage separately.
crit.$capNote: Levels run to 99; chance is flat at maxChance from capLevel onward.
crit.$damageNote: PROVISIONAL. Placeholder inherited from lib/damage.js; never stated in the design.

moveDelivery.$comment: Every move has exactly one delivery class. The class decides contact, which is what abilities like Thorns key off.

classes.name: Punch
classes.note: Struck with a limb or appendage.

classes.name: Body
classes.note: The whole creature is the weapon. Height and weight feed these.

classes.name: Voice
classes.note: Sound. Reaches things a projectile would not.

classes.name: Trap
classes.note: Placed rather than aimed; resolves on a condition.

size.$comment: Flavour first, but some moves read them. Metric, per species.
size.$capNote: PROPOSED. Ceiling on any weight-ratio term in a damage calc, so a very heavy mon against a very light one cannot produce an unbounded multiplier.

energy.$comment: PROPOSED, not stated by the design. Energy persists between battles, so this is a resource-management system, not a pacing one. Numbers are a first cut; the shape is the part to argue with.
energy.$moveCostNote: Per-move energy cost is move data and does not exist yet; defaultMoveCost stands in.
energy.$floorNote: Exhausted is the FLOOR -- penalties stop deepening there, and Empty is no worse except that the mon cannot battle at all. Without this, low energy lowering stats and accuracy while raising cost is a positive feedback loop into losing.

restoration.$benchNote: A mon not in the active slot recovers a little each battle. This makes ROTATION the core management verb rather than item-spam.
restoration.$supportNote: Support mons can restore energy AND stamina. This is the in-battle answer to attrition and gives Light and Psychic a job that is always live, which Light in particular needed.

energy.$emptyNote: Energy reaching 0 KNOCKS THE MON OUT. Energy is therefore a second health bar, not a soft debuff -- there are two ways to lose a mon, and the Exhausted tier is genuinely dangerous rather than merely inconvenient.

affection.$comment: How attached a mon is to its trainer. Modifies stats by affection points and level, with extra effects at maximum. Per-instance state, not species data.
affection.blockedOn: Does affection apply in competitive play? A grindable stat bonus breaks any competitive format; the usual answer is that it applies in casual play and is normalised out of ranked.
affection.$note: Persistence was never in doubt; the open question is competitive play, and it is still open.

proxy.$comment: A proxy is anything that takes a mon's place: Jack-In-The-Box, a decoy, a summon, a substitute. The rule is deliberately absolute.
proxy.$blocksNote: ALL attacks hit the proxy, with no exceptions. Voice does not reach past it; neither does Trap, Ranged or anything else. The only counterplay to a proxy is not attacking.
openRules: Do non-damaging effects (status, stat drops, hazards) pass through to the mon behind it, or are those blocked too? 'Blocks all attacks' does not settle this.
When a hit breaks the proxy, does the excess damage carry through to the mon, or is it absorbed? Absorbed is the safer default.
Can a second proxy be summoned while one is standing? If yes, an untilDestroyed proxy is an unbounded stall engine.
Can a proxy be healed, and does it benefit from the summoner's abilities?

stamina.$comment: Per-move uses. Persists between battles, like energy. Distinct axis: stamina limits WHICH move, energy limits HOW LONG the mon can fight at all.
stamina.$maxUsesNote: Per-move data. Moves do not exist yet, so there is nothing to put here.
stamina.restoration: Same channels as energy: rest at base, items, and bench recovery.

struggle.$comment: What a mon does when every move is out of stamina. PROPOSED -- the design says 'a weak attack that deals recoil damage'; the numbers and the typing question are mine.
struggle.$typeNote: PROPOSED TYPELESS -- no STAB, no type effectiveness. If Struggle were Normal-typed it would deal ZERO to Phantom (Normal -> Phantom is 0), so a mon out of stamina could not touch a Phantom at all and both would sit there until energy killed them. Typeless avoids that dead end.
struggle.$deliveryNote: Contact, so Thorns punishes a flailing mon. A desperate lunge should hurt to make.
struggle.$costNote: Struggle still burns energy, so running out of stamina accelerates the run toward the energy KO.
